petite.label: Petite
petite.description: Under ~5'3" — proportion matters more than size
petite.silhouette: Keep lines vertical and unbroken; avoid anything that cuts you at the widest point.
tips: Knee-length kurtis and A-line anarkalis lengthen the frame; floor-sweeping flares swallow it.
Churidars or straight pants over wide palazzos; if you love palazzos, keep the kurta short.
Lighter, smaller prints and a single-colour saree drape read taller than big borders.

regular.label: Regular
regular.description: Average height and build — most cuts work
regular.silhouette: Balanced proportions; use fit to add shape and fabric to add drama.
tips: Straight kurtas with palazzos or churidars both work — choose by occasion.
Structured fabrics (raw silk, chanderi) hold a silhouette; georgette and chiffon flow.
Belt a saree or an anarkali at the waist for a sharper evening line.

tall.label: Tall
tall.silhouette: Horizontal interest and layers break up height gracefully.
tips: Wide palazzos and sharara sets look intentional on a long frame.
Bold borders, wide dupattas and contrast hems add horizontal balance.
Long kurtas need enough length — check they clear the knee or go full-length.

plus.label: Plus
plus.description: Curvier build — drape and structure over cling
plus.silhouette: Skim, don't cling; define the narrowest point; keep hemlines long and clean.
tips: Empire or under-bust anarkalis and long straight kurtas skim comfortably.
Medium-weight fabrics (cotton silk, chanderi, georgette) drape better than stiff brocade or clingy jersey.
V or deep-U necklines and three-quarter sleeves lengthen; avoid short kurtis that end at the hip.

slim.label: Slim
slim.description: Lean frame — add structure and breadth
slim.silhouette: Structured shoulders and layers add presence; avoid anything oversized or shapeless.
tips: A Nehru jacket over a kurta instantly adds shoulder and chest.
Bandhgalas and sherwanis should be tailored close — a boxy fit reads as borrowed.
Heavier fabrics (raw silk, velvet, brocade) add visual weight; skip flimsy rayon.

athletic.label: Athletic
athletic.description: Broad shoulders, narrow waist — tapered cuts
athletic.silhouette: Show the taper; avoid straight boxy cuts that hide it.
tips: Fitted kurtas with a side slit and churidar or straight pyjama show the frame.
Bandhgalas with a nipped waist are your best formal option.
Keep Nehru jackets slim — a wide waistcoat undoes the taper.

regular.label: Regular
regular.silhouette: Balanced; use fabric weight and layering to dress up or down.
tips: Cotton kurta-pyjama for day, silk kurta with a Nehru jacket for evenings.
A single well-fitted bandhgala covers receptions, sangeets and formal dinners.
Dhoti or veshti with a silk kurta for temple and South Indian weddings.

tall.label: Tall
tall.silhouette: Break up the vertical with layers and contrast; mind kurta and sleeve lengths.
tips: Long sherwanis and knee-length kurtas suit height; short kurtas look cropped.
A contrast Nehru jacket or stole breaks the length nicely.
Check pyjama and churidar length — off-the-rack often runs short.

broad.label: Broad
broad.description: Wider chest and midsection — clean vertical lines
broad.silhouette: Vertical lines, darker solids and open layers; avoid tight or heavily embellished pieces.
tips: Straight-cut kurtas in matte fabrics (cotton, linen, khadi) drape without clinging.
An open Nehru jacket creates a slimming vertical panel.
Choose fine embroidery over all-over brocade; keep the shine for accessories.

plus.label: Plus
plus.description: Larger build — comfort and drape first
plus.silhouette: Skimming fits, breathable mid-weight fabrics, long unbroken lines.
tips: Long kurtas with straight pyjamas; avoid churidars that bunch.
Darker solids and pinstripes; a Nehru jacket left open lengthens the torso.
A well-cut sherwani in a matte silk is more flattering than a fitted bandhgala.
